name: EventQL
tagline: Abandoned AGPL columnar SQL database for streaming event and time-series analytics, written in modern C++.
description: EventQL was a distributed columnar database for event, time-series and sensor analytics, open-sourced in 2016 by DeepCortex GmbH under the AGPL. Tables were automatically split into ordered key-range partitions spread across equal, shared-nothing nodes coordinated by ZooKeeper, with no shard count to choose up front. Primary-key based UPSERT made exactly-once ingestion from streams easy, columnar storage with REPEATED and RECORD types allowed nested JSON-like rows, and queries used nearly complete SQL 2009, including joins, with vectorised execution and SSE. It also offered JavaScript MapReduce, an HTTP API and a native TCP protocol. The last release, 0.4.1, shipped in February 2017 and development stopped soon after; ClickHouse covers the same ground today.
statusNote: Last release 0.4.1 (February 2017); no commits since May 2017. ClickHouse, Apache Druid or Apache Pinot fill this role today.

scale.notes: Automatic key-range partitioning across shared-nothing nodes; vendor claimed petabyte-scale tables.

strengths: Automatic range partitioning: no shard count to pick up front
Idempotent primary-key UPSERT simplifies exactly-once ingestion from streams
Nested REPEATED/RECORD columns for JSON-like event data
Joins and near-complete SQL 2009 on a columnar engine
weaknesses: Abandoned since 2017; no security fixes or maintained builds
AGPL licence complicates embedding in hosted products
Small community; documentation site eventql.io is offline
useCases: Historical reference for columnar event-analytics engine design
Reading a compact C++ implementation of range-partitioned columnar storage
